subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: How Rockets Work: Newton in Space
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: How Rockets Work: Newton in Space.

hook.text: A rocket doesn't push against air. It throws mass backward, and Newton's third law pushes it forward.

buildup.text: The rocket equation — Tsiolkovsky's equation — shows that most of a rocket's weight must be fuel. The Saturn V was 85% propellant.

discovery.text: Specific impulse measures engine efficiency. Chemical rockets max out around 450 seconds. Ion engines reach 10,000 seconds.

twist.text: Ion engines produce incredible efficiency but tiny thrust. They can't lift off Earth but can accelerate for months in space.

climax.text: Multi-stage rockets discard empty tanks during flight. Shedding dead weight is the only way chemical rockets can reach orbit.

punchline.text: Throw stuff backward. Go forward. Dump the empty tanks. Repeat.

quiz.question: Why do rockets use multiple stages?
options: Each stage uses a different type of fuel optimized for that altitude
Shedding empty tanks reduces dead weight, allowing chemical rockets to reach orbit
Multiple engines are needed because a single engine can't burn long enough
